title: Continuous coefficient filtration with admissible geometric strata
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$, and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]; noetherian means locally noetherian and quasi-compact, dimension is the supremum of lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets, and invertibility means that $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring. On the fixed small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_T$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_T=B_T[1/\varpi]$. These are canonically the continuous-function ring sheaves $V\mapsto C(|V|,A)$ and $V\mapsto C(|V|,E)$, respectively, with constant-section coefficient maps [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. Modules and tensor products mean sheaf modules and sheaf tensor products [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A continuous-constructible integral module has a finite locally closed stratification on which it is pro-etale locally $B_T\otimes_A P$ for a finitely presented $A$-module $P$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module, def-constructible-stratification]. An $E_X$-module $F$ is rational constructible if a finite locally closed stratification makes it pro-etale locally free of finite rank. Under the canonical continuous-coefficient realization and the internal/sectionwise module equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], such $F$ corresponds to a constructible module over $p_X^*C(-,E)$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-constructible]. These equivalences identify the local model $E_T^r$ with the finite constant model $p_T^*C(-,E)\otimes_E E^r$, preserve the underlying abelian sheaves, and are compatible with locally closed coefficient restriction. There exist $m\geq0$, open subschemes $\varnothing=V_0\subset\cdots\subset V_m=X$, and reduced closed immersions $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$ with underlying sets $V_k\setminus V_{k-1}$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The $V_k$ and $S_k$ are noetherian, have dimension at most $\dim X$, and have $\ell$ invertible. Each $v_k:V_k\hookrightarrow X$ and each open complement of $t_k$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Using the actual module functors [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], the counits identify $F_k=v_{k!}v_k^*F$ with subobjects of $F$, giving
$$0=F_0\subset\cdots\subset F_m=F,\qquad F_k/F_{k-1}\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k,$$
where $L_k=t_k^*(F|_{V_k})$ is pro-etale locally free of finite rank over $E_{S_k}$. The coefficient restrictions and these module functors are the continuous sectionwise ones under the preceding identifications. Empty $X$, rank zero, and $m=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.3, 6.8.6 and 6.8.10, pp. 59-60; finite-stratum reduction in Lemma 6.8.13 and Proposition 6.8.14(2); coefficient identification Lemma 6.8.2

proof.text: First obtain a Noetherian underlying space: the minimal-closed-subset assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] rules out an infinite strictly descending chain (the set of its terms would have no minimal member). Set $\Lambda=C(-,E)$. The coefficient comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations], the integral/localized identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction], and [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] identify the reconstructed section-ring sheaf of $p_T^*\Lambda$ with $E_T$. In finite free coordinates the scalar-model identification is $e\otimes(c_i)_i\mapsto(ec_i)_i$, with inverse $(e_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes\epsilon_i$. These formulas use constant scalar sections and commute with restriction, so define inverse sheaf-module maps. Evaluating at the point gives the scalar ring $\Lambda(*)=C(*,E)=E$. For each stratum immersion $\iota_a$ the comparison $\mathcal E\,\iota^*_{a,\rm int}\cong\iota^*_{a,\rm sec}\mathcal E$ (with $\mathcal E$ the internal/sectionwise equivalence) of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], with the ring isomorphisms just named, identifies the internal restriction of $F^c$ with the given $F|_{X_a}$, and restriction to the members of a pro-etale cover is the localization of both sites. Consequently the given rational constructibility stratification and its local models $E_T^r$ give a constructible internal $p_X^*\Lambda$-module $F^c$ in the finite constant model sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. No assertion that all sections of a sheaf tensor product are elementary tensors is used.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2; Definitions 6.8.3 and 6.8.6; paragraph before Definition 6.8.6 (locally closed restriction).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-model-stratum-filtration] to $X$, $\Lambda=C(-,E)$ and $F^c$. Its hypotheses are exactly the Noetherian underlying space and finite scalar local models established in Step 1; it requires no finite type hypothesis on $X$. It gives $m$, the ordered opens $V_k$, reduced closed strata $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$ with underlying sets $V_k\setminus V_{k-1}$, and finite constant models for $L_k^c=t_k^*((F^c)|_{V_k})$. It also gives every required qcqs open immersion, the monic counits and the filtration quotient isomorphisms in the internal category.

source.place: Tag 09Y5, lemma-noetherian-partition-refined-by-stratification; existing sheaf extraction lem-sfb-finite-model-stratum-filtration, whose statement includes reduced strata, qcqs opens and counit quotients.

proof.text: On a trivializing cover of each $S_k$, its scalar model is $p_T^*C(-,E)\otimes_E P$ for a finitely presented $E$-module $P$. The field clause of [lem-sfb-scalar-finite-free-resolutions] supplies an isomorphism $E^r\cong P$ with $r\geq0$. Tensor this isomorphism and its inverse with the coefficient ring; their composites are identities by the tensor universal property. The coordinate maps of Step 1 identify the result with $E_T^r$. The inverse-image comparisons $\mathcal E\,t^*_{k,\rm int}\cong t^*_{k,\rm sec}\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E\,v^*_{k,\rm int}\cong v^*_{k,\rm sec}\mathcal E$ of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] carry $L_k^c$ to the sectionwise restriction. Thus the corresponding sectionwise $L_k=t_k^*(F|_{V_k})$ is pro-etale locally free of finite rank. A scalar module of rank zero gives the zero local model, as required.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.3 and 6.8.6, comparing finite constant scalar models over the field E with lisse models.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] to these internal functors. It identifies inverse image, ordinary closed direct image, and open extension by zero with their sectionwise ringed-topos versions, identifies their adjunction units and counits, and is an exact equivalence. The coefficient restriction isomorphisms in [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] are compatible with composition and the scalar map, so the rings in these comparisons are the specified continuous $E_T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] the actual open extension in the question is left adjoint to that inverse image; hence it is the open functor in this comparison, with the same counit. It follows that the internal monic counit is precisely $v_{k!}v_k^*F\to F$ after these specified comparisons. Exactness of the equivalence identifies its subobject, all successive quotients, and the two endpoints. Thus $0=F_0\subset\cdots\subset F_m=F$ and $F_k/F_{k-1}\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$ for the actual continuous sectionwise functors; the underlying abelian sheaves are retained.

proof.text: Each $V_k$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. In particular it has a cover by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ Noetherian. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], their inverse images under $t_k$ are $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$. Every ideal $J$ of $R/I$ is the image of its inverse image in $R$; the images of finitely many generators of that inverse image generate $J$. Thus $R/I$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and these inverse images make $S_k$ locally Noetherian in the sense of [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Finally $|S_k|$ is a closed subset of the quasi-compact $|V_k|$: add its open complement to any ambient open cover to obtain a finite subcover. Hence $S_k$ is quasi-compact and Noetherian. This is the elementary closed-subscheme case of Stacks Tag 02IK, with the quotient-ring and compactness arguments displayed.

source.place: Tag 02IK, lemma-locally-closed-in-Noetherian; closed case proved directly. Open input: Tag 01OW, lemma-locally-Noetherian.

proof.text: The open-subspace bound [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone], applied to $V_k\subseteq X$, gives $\dim V_k\leq\dim X$. Since $t_k$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset [def-weil-closed-immersion], a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $S_k$ is a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $V_k$. Taking suprema gives $\dim S_k\leq\dim V_k\leq\dim X$. Thus both are finite-dimensional; reducedness was already part of Step 2. At a point of $V_k$ the local ring equals that of $X$ by [def-weil-open-immersion], and the local-ring map from $V_k$ to $S_k$ sends units to units. The inverse of $\ell$ in the first local ring therefore maps to an inverse in the second. This proves invertibility of $\ell$ on both kinds of subscheme without a regularity or equidimensionality assumption.

source.place: Tag 0055, definition-Krull and following open-monotonicity remark; closed-subspace chain inclusion is immediate from the definition.

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, use $m=0$ and the empty filtration: the sheaf condition for the empty covering makes every module on the empty site zero, so its two endpoints agree. Otherwise Step 2 supplies the finite chain. No inclusion was required to be strict, and zero local models are permitted by Step 3. All identities and comparisons above therefore also cover rank zero and any zero quotient.

Steps 5-6 are genuinely elementary: R/I is noetherian, a closed subset of a quasi-compact space is quasi-compact, open-subspace dimension bound plus closed chains, local-ring units go to units.
